title: Loki backend cannot sync rule groups on home cluster (namespace-scheme vs Loki router collision)
description:
Task 24 e2e run (docs/e2e.md §4) found: this operator's namespace scheme
(rulesNamespacePrefix/CR-namespace/CR-name, e.g. e2e/e2e/homelab) always
embeds a literal '/'. On this cluster's Loki 3.6.7, the ruler HTTP
router 404s on any per-namespace/per-group route (GET-single, POST
create/replace, and by the same logic DELETE) once the namespace
contains an embedded '/' -- confirmed independently of the operator
with direct curl, both through the gateway and hitting Loki directly.
Only the bulk GET /loki/api/v1/rules works. Mimir's ruler is
unaffected (same multi-segment namespace shape syncs fine).

Production tenant 1's existing Loki rules already work around this by
using a single-segment namespace (loki-homelab, no embedded '/'),
almost certainly written directly to the ruler's S3 store rather than
through this API.

Consequence: the Loki backend of alerts-operator is non-functional on
this cluster as currently namespaced. Needs a design decision:
(a) a Loki-specific namespace join character that avoids embedded '/'
    when backend: loki (e.g. join with '.' or '-' instead of '/'), or
(b) investigate/upgrade this Loki deployment's ruler routing.
(a) is the lower-risk fix since it's entirely within this project's
control; (b) depends on infra outside this repo.

Full investigation and evidence: docs/e2e.md §4,
.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-21-alerts-operator/task-24-report.md.

title: docs/e2e.md-style multi-file sed | kubectl apply silently drops content without --- separator
description: Passing two filenames to sed and piping into kubectl apply -f - concatenates the two YAML docs with no --- separator, so kubectl merges the two flat mappings into one object (later duplicate keys win) -- one of the two objects silently never gets created. Found in task 24's e2e run applying alertrulegroup-mimir.yaml + alertrulegroup-loki.yaml together (docs/e2e.md originally, an earlier draft, later fixed). Audit any other doc/example that concatenates multiple example YAML files this way and either insert an explicit --- between files or apply them separately.

title: Crash between Alertmanager store.Set and the status patch can strand a config
description: syncAlertmanager writes the Alertmanager document to Mimir, then patches status with alertmanagerConfigHash/alertmanagerConfigAddress as the record that this Tenant owns it. A crash in between leaves the document written but unrecorded. Since Task 20's fix gates finalizer cleanup on that recorded hash, a Tenant deleted while in that state leaves the config behind with no CR describing it. Self-heals on any normal retry, because the next sync re-confirms via store.Get and records the hash. Found by Codex during Task 20 fix round 1 and parked deliberately: closing it needs write-ahead intent in status before the backend call, which is a design change, not a patch.

title: Missing basic-auth Secret wedges a deleting Tenant in Terminating
description: If a Tenant's BasicAuthSecretRef target is gone when the Tenant is deleted, backendOptions cannot resolve credentials, finalize cannot reach the backend, and the retry-forever policy keeps the object Terminating indefinitely. Probe-confirmed by the Task 20 reviewer; recovers as soon as the Secret is restored. The retry-forever policy itself is accepted and correct — this is a new trigger for it that operators will hit by deleting a namespace's Secret before the Tenant. Chart/docs task should cover it: document the recovery (recreate the Secret) and consider ordering guidance so the Secret outlives the Tenant.
close_reason: Documented in docs/migration.md Appendix B: recovering a Tenant stuck Terminating (recovery: recreate the basicAuthSecretRef Secret; ordering: delete Tenant before its auth Secret). Task 22.

title: Residual TOCTOU in finalizer ownership tie-break under simultaneous deletion
description: finalizeOwner()/claimants() read Tenants through an uncached APIReader and pick a deterministic lowest-name winner so exactly one of two colliding Tenants performs cleanup. A narrow window survives: if two already-colliding Tenants are deleted with sub-second overlap, both can observe the other as still present (or both as absent) and either double-clean or skip. Documented by the Task 20 implementer under 'Known accepted residual'. Closing it needs real cross-reconcile coordination (lease or a claim annotation), which was out of Task 20's scope. Impact is bounded: cleanup is idempotent deletes, so a double-clean is harmless; the skip case leaves backend state behind with no CR to retry it.

title: Enqueue peer Tenants when an ownership-key collision clears
description: When two Tenants collide on tenantId+backend+prefix, pruning is disabled on both and each reports RulesSynced=False/Conflict. If the conflicting Tenant is then deleted, or changes its (mutable) backend address, only that Tenant is enqueued — the surviving one stays Conflict with pruning disabled until its next resyncInterval (default 5m). Found by Codex during Task 19 fix round 1 (tenant_rules.go:213-216). Bounded and self-healing, and errs safe: nothing is wrongly deleted, and the arrival direction has no destructive window since a peer CR exists before its namespaces do. Fix: a watch mapper enqueueing affected peers on Tenant change. Needs its own design pass — a naive mapper amplifies every Tenant status write into a fan-out across all Tenants sharing a backend.
notes: Task 20 adds a sibling case: when the finalizer skips cleanup because another Tenant is the deterministic claimant, that claimant is not enqueued either, so it does not learn the conflict cleared until its next resync. Same mechanism, same fix (a peer-enqueue watch mapper) — resolve both together.

title: Recompute Alertmanager auth fingerprint after syncRules (TOCTOU)
description: syncAlertmanager resolves backend credentials, then syncRules runs a full List + POST-per-changed-group + DELETEs against Mimir before the second credential resolution. The window between the two resolutions is seconds, not microseconds, and is widest exactly when the backend is slow or unhealthy. Found by Codex during Task 19, parked by the implementer on a 'microsecond window' argument the task reviewer disproved. Impact is bounded: at most one resync interval of staleness, and a missing secret fails safe. Fix: have authFingerprint take backend.Options (it is Task 19's own new function, so no pinned signature blocks this) and recompute after syncRules.

title: deploy-dev: consider auto-applying refreshed CRDs and a real uninstall guard
description:
Codex review (task 24, round 1 + round 2) flagged two real but
low-severity gaps in the deploy-dev/undeploy-dev Makefile targets,
which were left as-is because their exact content is binding per the
task 24 brief and matches already-documented chart behavior:

1. deploy-dev (Makefile:169-175): helm upgrade skips crds/ once a
   release exists, so a schema/CEL change isn't picked up on redeploy.
   Already documented in the chart's own install NOTES.txt with the
   manual remediation. Consider having deploy-dev apply
   charts/alerts-operator/crds/*.yaml with kubectl apply --server-side
   before the helm upgrade, so this is automatic.
2. undeploy-dev (Makefile:177-178): `helm uninstall ... || true`
   swallows every failure, not just "release not found". Consider
   using helm's own ignore-not-found equivalent instead of a blanket
   `|| true`.
3. Mutable :dev tag + pullPolicy Always won't force a rollout on an
   unchanged pod spec if redeployed at the default DEV_IMG_TAG=dev.
   Already mitigated by recommending a pinned sha tag (which is what
   task 24's actual run used); consider whether deploy-dev should
   force a rollout restart regardless of tag.

None of this blocked task 24's actual e2e run (which used a pinned
sha tag throughout). Low priority polish.

title: purge-dev-crds negative-secret-deletion runbook step: document the ExternalSecret-break technique
description: docs/e2e.md §3's negative test found that kubectl delete secret <name> alone doesn't reliably reproduce SecretNotFound when the secret is owned by an ExternalSecret with creationPolicy: Owner -- ESO recreates it in ~1-2s. The runbook now documents breaking the ExternalSecret's remoteRef.key first to get a stable window. Low priority: just keep this technique in docs/e2e.md if the runbook is re-run; no code change implied.

value: Never wait on a process with pgrep -f "<string>" when the waiting shell's own command line contains <string> — pgrep -f matches full command lines, so the wait loop matches itself and never exits. Cost us 87min: a subagent ran 'until ! pgrep -f "codex exec review"; do sleep 5; done' after launching codex, and four such loops deadlocked. Wait on the PID (wait $!) or match a pattern the loop cannot contain.

In bash, 'set -e' does NOT abort on a negated command: '! grep -q X file' never fails the script, whatever the result. Every 'must not contain X' assertion written that way is silently inert. Found in alerts-operator's chart-test (an injected fake webhook config passed the no-webhook check). Use explicit 'if grep -q X f; then echo FAIL; exit 1; fi' instead. Same trap applies to any '! cmd' and to commands in a pipeline that is not the last element.
